## AI & Mathematics

### <span class="imp imp-high" title="Importance 7/10" aria-label="Importance 7 of 10">7</span> Anthropic researcher and NYU mathematician claim Claude-assisted Navier-Stokes proof
On November 20, 2026, Levent Alpöge (Anthropic mathematician) and Tristan Buckmaster (NYU professor) posted a 79-page paper claiming to prove finite-time blowup for the 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations without external force. The authors state: "We used Anthropic models (Claude) throughout this work," and no independent mathematician has yet verified the result.

<ul class="takeaways">
<li>79-page proof claims to resolve Millennium Prize problem</li>
<li>Constructs discretely self-similar solution with blowup rate (T - t)^(-1/4)</li>
<li>Explicitly states &quot;We used Anthropic models (Claude) throughout this work&quot;</li>
<li>Certificate released (hash provided; full certificate not public)</li>
<li>No independent verification yet; criticism of OpenAI&#x27;s September 2026 proof noted</li>
</ul>

Sources: [MLQ.ai](https://news.google.?oc=5) <span class="src-badge src-research">AI Web Searched</span>

### <span class="imp imp-high" title="Importance 7/10" aria-label="Importance 7 of 10">7</span> Claude AI Assists Mathematician in Solving 167-Year-Old Mathematical Problem
An Anthropic mathematician used Claude to help verify a proof solving a century-and-a-half-old open problem.

<ul class="takeaways">
<li>Alpöge&#x27;s proof formalized in Lean; developed with Claude assistance</li>
<li>Independent Stanford proof (Masullo and Vakil) explicitly &quot;all human, no AI&quot;</li>
<li>167-year-old conjecture dating to 1859; $1 million Millennium Prize</li>
<li>Mathematics community reviewing both claimed solutions</li>
<li>Proof formalized in Lean programming language</li>
<li>Addresses Generalized Riemann Hypothesis variant</li>
<li>Announced November 20, 2026, one day after Anthropic&#x27;s IPO</li>
<li>Conjecture proposed 1859 by Bernhard Riemann; $1 million bounty</li>
</ul>
